name: Boise River Mule Deer Migration
source: Boise River Migration Statistics and seasonal migration routes map, analyzed / prepared by Jodi Berg and Scott Bergen, January 2020
summary: Boise River mule deer use areas of the foothills west of Lucky Peak Reservoir in winter. Mule deer wintering in this area typically traverse the Boise River Valley into reaches much farther up the valley, and may travel as far as the Sawtooth Mountains. On average, Boise River mule deer travel over 45 miles to migrate between summer and winter range, with the farthest individuals traveling close to 96 miles. Deer must navigate State Highway 21 near Lucky Peak Reservoir, an area where wildlife-vehicle collisions have regularly occurred in late fall, winter, and early spring. However, recent and upcoming infrastructure improvement projects are mitigating some of those issues. Deer must also navigate Lucky Peak and Arrowrock Reservoirs, an issue primarily related to ice formation at key crossing points. The population of wintering mule deer in the greater area (including the Blacks Creek population) was estimated at 28,600 in January 2018.
methods: Of 119 individual seasonal migrations, 3 used Brownian bridge movement models with an 8-hour time-lag, 19 used forced motion variance (1000 m) with a 14-hour time-lag, and 97 used forced motion variance (1000 m) with a 27-hour time-lag.
